questions.stem: A sample exam on rotating the budget line sets out the question below. income 60, Px falls to 3; X-intercept?
questions.explanation: 60/3=20. Using income 60 as intercept is wrong. A price change pivots the budget line around the intercept for the unaffected good, changing the slope but not that intercept. Shifting the whole line parallel is the common mistake.

questions.stem: explain why ordinal utility suffices for consumer theory.

answer.exemplar: Consumer theory needs only preference orderings to predict choices, which ordinal utility provides.

questions.explanation: For a why ordinal utility is enough question like this, the governing rule is: Orderings suffice. Applying it gives "Consumer theory needs only preference orderings to predict choices, which ordinal utility provides" as the answer.

questions.stem: A policy brief on diminishing marginal utility as a shared regularity asks an analyst to evaluate the market evidence below. diminishing marginal utility explains why?

options.misconception: denies substitution

questions.explanation: Diminishing MU encourages diversification. Buying one good, ignoring prices, or no substitution are wrong.

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.stem: A firm's planning memo records the following numbers. income 75, Px=5; X-intercept?
questions.explanation: 75/5=15. Multiplying gives 375. A budget constraint requires total spending on all goods to equal income, so quantities are limited by prices and income together. Ignoring one good's spending is the common slip.

options.text: MU equals price for each good.

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.stem: An assignment on marginal-utility-per-dollar rule gives the following case for analysis. MUx/Px=3, MUy/Py=5; reallocate how?

options.misconception: names "Keep bundle unchanged" where the rule requires "Buy more Y and less X"

options.text: Buy more Y and less X.
Buy more X and less Y.
options.misconception: reverses reallocation
Overreacts to the change by asserting buy neither good.

questions.explanation: The rule that settles this the marginal-utility-per-dollar rule item is: Shift to higher ratio. That is why "Buy more Y and less X" is right. The option "Keep bundle unchanged" (names "Keep bundle unchanged" where the rule requires "Buy more Y and less X") does not satisfy the rule.

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.stem: explain rotation of budget line from a price increase.

answer.exemplar: The intercept of the dearer good falls while the other intercept stays, pivoting the line inward.

questions.explanation: Applying the rotating the budget line rule — One intercept falls — yields "The intercept of the dearer good falls while the other intercept stays, pivoting the line inward". Reversing the reasoning would recover the given quantities.

questions.stem: Which description of diminishing marginal utility is correct?

options.text: A law that always holds exactly.

questions.explanation: For a diminishing marginal utility as a shared regularity question like this, the governing rule is: Common regularity.
